name: What patio cover size is exempt in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What size patio cover or pergola can be built without a permit in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What size patio cover or pergola can be built without a permit in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most commonly cited exemption in the Los Angeles area is for a detached one-story accessory structure with no more than 120 square feet of roof area. That does not automatically cover every pergola or patio cover, especially if the structure is attached to the home, includes a solid roof, or needs electrical, plumbing, or foundation work. In practice, homeowners should not rely on size alone. The project’s attachment, height, setbacks, and utility connections often matter as much as square footage. For outdoor living projects, it is smart to confirm the current local interpretation before ordering materials or pouring footings, because a structure that looks small can still trigger plan check.
acceptedAnswer.description: A detached one-story accessory structure not exceeding 120 square feet of roof area may be exempt in Los Angeles County. Larger structures, attached covers, or projects with utilities usually require permit review.
